name: Landline: a terminal for your own machines
description:
Landline is a terminal for the machines you already own, reached over your own Tailscale network. A small open source daemon runs on Mac, Linux or Windows, and the app gives you a real shell on each. No SSH keys, no open ports, no account, and nothing of ours in between.

Version 1.5 is built for checking on long jobs and coding agents from the phone. When a program rings the terminal bell or sends a notification, the host list marks that machine as waiting on you. Sessions survive network changes with scrollback intact. Open any machine from Shortcuts, Spotlight, Siri or the Action button, and answer an agent with one-tap keys.

Made for iPhone Duo and iPad. Text now follows Dynamic Type, and every screen passes an automated VoiceOver audit for labels and traits. Paid once, no subscription.
notes: Open source under MIT, daemon and app: github.com/mhrsntrk/landline. No telemetry, no analytics SDK, no accounts. Store listing in 10 locales; the app UI is English. Trying it needs a Tailscale tailnet and one machine running the daemon; happy to arrange a walkthrough.
